summary: Around 1:30 a.m. on August 2 or 3, 1965, Mr. A. L. Smith and other individuals in Tulsa, Oklahoma, reported seeing a UFO that displayed multiple colors. A photograph reportedly taken of the object is suspected to be inauthentic [4, 7].
title: **Multicolor UFO Sighted in Tulsa, Oklahoma**

name: **Project Blue Book Attempts Explanation for Oklahoma Sightings**
description: **August 2:** Project Blue Book issues a press release attempting to explain the **August 1 sightings as astronomical objects**, contradicted by an astronomer [7].
summary: On August 2, 1965, Project Blue Book released a statement to the press, suggesting that the numerous UFO sightings reported on August 1st could be attributed to conventional astronomical phenomena. This explanation was subsequently disputed by an astronomer [7].
title: **Project Blue Book Attempts Explanation for Oklahoma Sightings**

name: **Unidentified Radar Blips Detected at Wichita Airport**
description: **August 2, 2:30 a.m. onwards:** **Unidentified radar blips are detected at Wichita Municipal Airport in Kansas** [4, 7].
summary: Starting at 2:30 a.m. on August 2, 1965, the radar system at Wichita Municipal Airport in Kansas began detecting unidentified signals or blips [4, 7].
title: **Unidentified Radar Blips Detected at Wichita Airport**

name: "Mercury Capsule" Shaped Object Photographed in Texas**
description: **August 2, 3:00 a.m.:** News photographer Robert Campbell in **Texas** photographs a **stationary object described as "Mercury capsule" shaped** [4, 7].
summary: On August 2, 1965, at 3:00 a.m., Robert Campbell, a news photographer in Texas, captured an image of a motionless object in the sky that was described as resembling the shape of a Mercury space capsule [4, 7].
title: "Mercury Capsule" Shaped Object Photographed in Texas**

name: **Fiery Sphere Emerges from Red Sea, Causes Large Wave**
description: **August 2:** The crew of the Russian steamship Raduga in the **Red Sea** witnesses a **fiery sphere emerge from the water, causing a large wave** [7].
summary: On August 2, 1965, the crew aboard the Russian steamship Raduga, sailing in the Red Sea, reported seeing a bright, spherical object on fire emerge from the water, which subsequently generated a significant wave [7].
title: **Fiery Sphere Emerges from Red Sea, Causes Large Wave**

name: **Silvery Discs Hovering in Seattle**
description: **August 10, 8:00 p.m.:** Francis C. Jennings and his wife in **Seattle** see **two silvery discs hovering** [4, 7].
summary: On August 10, 1965, at 8:00 p.m., Francis C. Jennings and his wife in Seattle, Washington, observed two disc-shaped objects that appeared to be silvery in color and were hovering in the sky [4, 7].
title: **Silvery Discs Hovering in Seattle**

name: **Disc Lands, Small Being Observed in Iowa**
description: **August 11?, 3:30 p.m.:** David Gibson in **Iowa** sees a **disc-shaped object land and briefly observes a small "being"** [4, 7].
summary: Around 3:30 p.m. on a day believed to be August 11, 1965, David Gibson in Iowa reported witnessing a disc-shaped object descend and land, during which time he briefly saw a small entity or "being" [4, 7].
title: **Disc Lands, Small Being Observed in Iowa**

name: **UFO Makes Erratic Movements Near Springfield, Ohio**
description: **August 12, 11:15 a.m.:** Maj. Jack D. Bond near **Springfield, Ohio**, sees a **UFO making erratic movements at high speed** [4, 7].
summary: On August 12, 1965, at 11:15 a.m., Major Jack D. Bond in the vicinity of Springfield, Ohio, observed an unidentified flying object performing irregular maneuvers at a high velocity [4, 7].
title: **UFO Makes Erratic Movements Near Springfield, Ohio**

name: **Disc Near Moon Causes Temporary Blindness and Sunburn-Like Effects**
description: **August 13, 9:30 p.m.?:** Leonard Chalupiak in **Pennsylvania** sees a **disc-shaped object near the moon and experiences temporary blindness and sunburn-like effects** [4, 7].
summary: Around 9:30 p.m. on a date believed to be August 13, 1965, Leonard Chalupiak in Pennsylvania reported observing a disc-shaped object in close proximity to the moon and subsequently experienced a period of temporary blindness along with symptoms resembling sunburn [4, 7].
title: **Disc Near Moon Causes Temporary Blindness and Sunburn-Like Effects**

name: **Domed Disc on Road Emits Flames in South Africa**
description: **September 16, Just after 12:00 midnight:** Police officers in **South Africa** see a **domed, disc-shaped object on the road that emits flames upon takeoff, leaving burned marks** [7, 8].
summary: Shortly after midnight on September 16, 1965, police officers in South Africa witnessed a disc-shaped object with a dome resting on the road. As it ascended, it emitted flames and left scorch marks on the ground [7, 8].
title: **Domed Disc on Road Emits Flames in South Africa**

name: **UFO Hovers Over Spain, Observed by Pilot**
description: **September 17:** A **UFO is seen hovering over Medina del Campo, Spain; a pilot observes it from his light plane** [7, 8].
summary: On September 17, 1965, an unidentified flying object was observed hovering over Medina del Campo in Spain. A pilot flying his light aircraft also witnessed the object [7, 8].
title: **UFO Hovers Over Spain, Observed by Pilot**

name: **Rocket-Like Object and Entities Encountered in Minnesota**
description: **October 23, Night:** Radio announcer James F. Townsend in **Minnesota** encounters a **rocket-like object with small entities nearby, experiencing car malfunction and a humming sound** [7, 8].
summary: During the night of October 23, 1965, James F. Townsend, a radio announcer in Minnesota, reported an encounter with an object resembling a rocket, in the vicinity of which he observed small entities. He also experienced a malfunction of his car and heard a humming noise [7, 8].
title: **Rocket-Like Object and Entities Encountered in Minnesota**

name: **Power Outages and Lights Observed in Minnesota**
description: **November 26, 8:00-9:00 p.m.:** **Power outages and observations of lights in the sky occur around St. Paul, Minnesota** [7].
summary: On November 26, 1965, between 8:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m., areas around St. Paul, Minnesota, experienced power failures, and simultaneous observations of unusual lights were reported in the sky [7].
title: **Power Outages and Lights Observed in Minnesota**

name: **Lighted Oval Object Lands in Nova Scotia, Smaller UFO Enters**
description: **November 30, 3:30 a.m.:** Seaman Ian Kinsey at **Canadian Forces Base Cornwallis in Nova Scotia** sees a **lighted oval object land on the beach, a smaller UFO enter it, and the larger object take off** [7, 8].
location: Canadian Forces Base Cornwallis, Nova Scotia, Canada
summary: On November 30, 1965, at 3:30 a.m., Seaman Ian Kinsey at Canadian Forces Base Cornwallis in Nova Scotia reported witnessing a luminous oval-shaped object land on the beach. Subsequently, a smaller unidentified flying object entered the larger one, which then ascended and flew away [7, 8].
title: **Lighted Oval Object Lands in Nova Scotia, Smaller UFO Enters**

name: **Two Saucers Face to Face Object Rises from Lagoon in Australia**
description: **January 19, Around 9:00 a.m.:** Banana grower George Pedley in **Tully, Queensland, Australia**, sees a **"two saucers face to face" shaped object rising from a lagoon, leaving a circular depression in the swamp grass**. Multiple similar "nests" are found in the area [8, 9].
summary: Around 9:00 a.m. on January 19, 1966, banana farmer George Pedley in Tully, Queensland, Australia, observed an object shaped like "two saucers face to face" ascending from a lagoon, leaving a circular mark in the swamp grass. Several other similar circular depressions, referred to as "nests," were discovered in the vicinity [8, 9].
title: **Two Saucers Face to Face Object Rises from Lagoon in Australia**

name: **Alleged UFO Sighting in Madrid, Later Confessed Hoax**
description: **February 6, Around 8:00 p.m.:** Several people in **Madrid, Spain**, allegedly see an unusual flying object. José Luis Jordán Peña claims a close view of a craft with legs and a symbol, **later confessing it was a hoax to prove paranoia** [8, 9].
summary: Around 8:00 p.m. on February 6, 1966, various individuals in Madrid, Spain, reportedly witnessed an unusual aerial object. José Luis Jordán Peña claimed to have had a close observation of a craft featuring legs and a symbol, but he subsequently admitted that his account was a fabrication intended to demonstrate public paranoia about UFOs [8, 9].
title: **Alleged UFO Sighting in Madrid, Later Confessed Hoax**

name: **Contactee Williamson Reports Seeing Three Large UFOs in Florida**
description: **March 22, Morning:** Contactee George Hunt Williamson in **Key West, Florida**, sees **three large UFOs with flashing lights** [8, 9].
summary: On the morning of March 22, 1966, George Hunt Williamson, a contactee, reported observing three large unidentified flying objects emitting flashing lights while in Key West, Florida [8, 9].
title: **Contactee Williamson Reports Seeing Three Large UFOs in Florida**

name: **Multiple Witnesses See Three UFOs in Key West, Florida**
description: **March 22, 10:00 p.m.:** Several people in **Key West, Florida**, see **three UFOs with flashing lights** [9].
summary: On March 22, 1966, at 10:00 p.m., a number of individuals in Key West, Florida, reported observing three unidentified flying objects that were emitting flashing lights [9].
title: **Multiple Witnesses See Three UFOs in Key West, Florida**

name: **Wingless Aircraft Blocks Road in Oklahoma**
description: **March 23, 5:05 a.m.:** William E. 'Eddie' Laxson in **Oklahoma** encounters a **wingless, fish-shaped aircraft blocking the road and sees a figure on it** [8, 9].
summary: On March 23, 1966, at 5:05 a.m., William E. 'Eddie' Laxson in Oklahoma reported encountering a wingless aircraft resembling a fish that was obstructing the road. He also claimed to have seen a figure on or near the object [8, 9].
title: **Wingless Aircraft Blocks Road in Oklahoma**

name: **Disc-Shaped Objects Seen Flying in Formation in Colorado**
description: **March 23, 5:00 p.m.:** Multiple witnesses in **Trinidad, Colorado**, see **two disc-shaped objects flying in formation** [9].
summary: On March 23, 1966, at 5:00 p.m., several individuals in Trinidad, Colorado, reported observing two disc-shaped objects flying together in a structured formation [9].
title: **Disc-Shaped Objects Seen Flying in Formation in Colorado**

name: **Elliptical Object Affects Car Near Bangor, Maine**
description: **March 23, 11:50 p.m.:** John T. King near **Bangor, Maine**, sees an **elliptical object that affects his car's lights and radio; he fires at it, and it speeds away** [8, 9].
summary: On March 23, 1966, at 11:50 p.m., John T. King, in the vicinity of Bangor, Maine, observed an elliptical-shaped object that appeared to interfere with his car's lights and radio. He then fired a weapon at the object, which subsequently departed at high speed [8, 9].
title: **Elliptical Object Affects Car Near Bangor, Maine**

name: **Hynek Investigates Michigan UFO Reports**
description: **March 23-25:** J. Allen Hynek investigates UFO reports in **Michigan**, including Dexter and Hillsdale, finding inconsistencies and media attention [8, 9].
summary: From March 23 to 25, 1966, J. Allen Hynek, a consultant to Project Blue Book, conducted an investigation into reported UFO sightings in Michigan, particularly in the areas of Dexter and Hillsdale. His findings included inconsistencies in the witness accounts, and the events garnered significant attention from the media [8, 9].
title: **Hynek Investigates Michigan UFO Reports**

name: **Cigar-Shaped Object Seen Over Crane Beach**
description: **Summer 1945** - Mrs. Helen Allen sees a '**long, silver-colored cigar**' that appears suddenly out of the haze above **Crane Beach in Ipswich, Massachusetts**. Huge and silent, it hovers low over the water not far from the shore. After a few seconds, it speeds away and disappears.
summary: In the summer of 1945, Mrs. Helen Allen observed a large, silent, silver cigar-shaped object hovering over Crane Beach before speeding away.
title: **Cigar-Shaped Object Seen Over Crane Beach**

name: **Army Air Force Approves YB-49 Redesignation**
description: **June 1, 1945** - The **Army Air Force approves a Northrop-recommended change for installing eight jet engines in each of two modified YB-35 piston-driven flying wings, which are redesignated YB-49s**.
summary: On June 1, 1945, the Army Air Force approved the redesignation of modified YB-35 flying wings to YB-49s, incorporating eight jet engines each.
title: **Army Air Force Approves YB-49 Redesignation**

name: **Tubular Object with Blue Flame Seen Over Morganton**
description: **June 1, 1945, 7:30 p.m.** - A **shiny, tubular object, 5-6 feet long**, is observed over **Morganton, North Carolina**. It streaks toward the northwest, **blue flame shooting from the rear**. After it vanishes in the mountains near **Lake James**, witnesses hear an explosion.
location: Morganton, North Carolina, USA; Lake James area, USA
summary: On June 1, 1945, at 7:30 p.m., a shiny, tubular object with a blue flame was seen over Morganton, North Carolina, streaking northwest before an explosion was heard near Lake James.
title: **Tubular Object with Blue Flame Seen Over Morganton**

name: **US Nuclear Stockpile in 1946**
description: **1946** - The **US nuclear stockpile consists of 9 atomic bombs**.
summary: In 1946, the United States had a nuclear stockpile of 9 atomic bombs.
title: **US Nuclear Stockpile in 1946**

name: **Square Lights Seen Over Istanbul**
description: **1946** - Dancers on the roof of a nightclub in **Istanbul, Turkey**, watch the rapid passage of **four square-shaped lights, reddish in color and aligned side by side**, moving from the east and disappearing in the west in less than 60 seconds. One witness, meteorologist and RAF pilot George Raymond Leatherbarrow, estimates their altitude at **50,000 feet** based on reflections on cirrus clouds.
summary: In 1946, four reddish, square-shaped lights were observed moving rapidly across the sky over Istanbul, Turkey, estimated at 50,000 feet by an RAF pilot.
title: **Square Lights Seen Over Istanbul**

name: **Abbot Predicts Communication with Venusians**
description: **1946** - American astrophysicist Charles Greeley Abbot writes that he thinks Earth might make contact with **Venusians**, coming into '**fluent communication by wireless with a race brought up completely separate, having their own systems of government, social usages, religions, and surrounded by vegetation and animals entirely unrelated to any here on earth**'.
summary: In 1946, American astrophysicist Charles Greeley Abbot predicted potential future wireless communication with Venusians, describing them as a completely separate race.
title: **Abbot Predicts Communication with Venusians**

name: **Westerham 'Contraption' Incident and Hoax Suspicions**
description: **1946** - A farmer named Gunyon in **Westerham, Kent, England**, calls the British Technical Intelligence staff asking that the Air Ministry come and remove one of these '**darned contraptions**' which has fallen on his farm. The intelligence officers ask for directions and are told to drive from **Croydon to Westerham**, turning onto a lane when they reach a pub called **The White Dog**. Amid great security, two staff cars are dispatched, but fail to find the farm. They locate a pub called **The White Hart** and a farmer named **Bunyan**, who strenuously denies having made the call. Although the incident appears to be a hoax, few people can reach the Technical Intelligence staff and convince them to make a field visit. Indeed, the intelligence officers believe that former Air Intelligence scientist Reginald Victor Jones, who has been skeptical of foo fighters and ghost rockets, is behind the affair. Jones writes that a signal is received from Gen. Douglas MacArthur's staff in Tokyo, asking for confirmation of a report that a **Russian flying bomb had recently crashed in England**. The other Director of Intelligence on the Air Staff, Air Commodore Roland Eugene Vintras, suggests to Jones that this might tie in with the '**Westerham Incident**'.
location: Westerham, Kent, England; Croydon, England; Tokyo, Japan
summary: In 1946, a report of a fallen 'contraption' in Westerham, England, led to a fruitless investigation, suspected as a hoax possibly linked to skepticism about ghost rockets or a report of a Russian flying bomb crash.
title: **Westerham 'Contraption' Incident and Hoax Suspicions**

name: **Report on German Flying Wings by Horten Brothers Issued**
description: **January 10, 1946** - The **Air Materiel Command at Wright Field, Ohio**, issues a restricted-access document, '**German Flying Wings Designed by Horten Brothers** by Capt. N. LeBlanc', detailing the drawings, photos, models, and documents relating to aircraft designed by Nazi aircraft designers the Horten brothers that were recovered in Germany by Allied forces.
summary: On January 10, 1946, the Air Materiel Command issued a report on German flying wings designed by the Horten brothers, based on materials recovered in Germany.

keywords: German Flying Wings Designed by Horten Brothers

title: **Report on German Flying Wings by Horten Brothers Issued**

name: **Project Diana Radar Echoes Off the Moon**
description: **January 10, 1946, 11:58 a.m.** - Harold D. Webb and Herbert P. Kauffman, scientists at **Project Diana** conducted by the US Army's Evans Signal Laboratory at **Fort Monmouth, New Jersey**, use a modified SCR-271 radar operating at 110 MHz with 3 kW peak-power to **bounce radar echoes off the Moon**. USAF Maj. Gen. Harold M. McClelland remarks to the press that this could be an '**opening step**' in communicating with intelligent life outside the Earth.
location: Fort Monmouth, New Jersey, USA; The Moon
summary: On January 10, 1946, Project Diana successfully bounced radar echoes off the Moon, leading to speculation about future communication with extraterrestrial life.
title: **Project Diana Radar Echoes Off the Moon**

name: **'Shooting Star' Maneuvers Over French Countryside**
description: **January 18, 1946, 11:00 p.m.** - A **US C-54 transport plane** is at **7,000 feet over the French countryside** on its way to **Paris, France**. Suddenly the pilot sees a brilliant '**shooting star**' about 35° above the horizon. It streaks down below the eastern horizon, then reappears and moves in a hyperbola before falling again.
location: French countryside (en route to Paris), France
summary: On January 18, 1946, at 11:00 p.m., the pilot of a US C-54 over the French countryside observed a brilliant 'shooting star' performing unusual hyperbolic maneuvers.
title: **'Shooting Star' Maneuvers Over French Countryside**

name: **4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron Reorganized**
description: **October 17, 1952** - The **4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron is reorganized to increase its strength**.
summary: On October 17, 1952, the 4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron underwent reorganization to expand its personnel.
title: **4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron Reorganized**

name: **Cigar-Shaped Structure and Round Objects with 'Angel's Hair' Seen Over Oloron, France**
description: **October 17, 1952, Early afternoon** - Residents of **Oloron-Sainte-Marie, Pyrénées-Atlantiques, France**, see a **large cigar-shaped structure** in the blue sky, inclined at a 45° angle. The witnesses include the family of Yves Prigent. A plume of white smoke is seen escaping from its upper end. At some distance in front of the cylinder, about **30 round, puffy objects with a central red spot** are following the same trajectory. The smaller objects move in pairs following a broken, zig-zag path. They leave an abundant trail of a **white substance (angel's hair)** behind them, which slowly falls to the ground as it disperses. For several hours, clumps of it hang on the trees, on the telephone wires, and on the roofs of houses.
summary: On the early afternoon of October 17, 1952, residents of Oloron, France, witnessed a large cigar-shaped object followed by about 30 round objects leaving trails of 'angel's hair'.
title: **Cigar-Shaped Structure and Round Objects with 'Angel's Hair' Seen Over Oloron, France**

name: **Cigar-Shaped Object with Sharp Turn Seen Over Adelaide Hills**
description: **October 18, 1952, 9:44 p.m.** - Journalist Keith Hooper is returning home from an assignment for the Adelaide Advertiser when he sees a **greenish-white, cigar-shaped object about the size of a Boeing 707** some 10 miles away over the **Adelaide Hills, South Australia**, moving southeast to northwest. The object makes a **sharp, right-angle turn upward**, recedes, then vanishes at tremendous speed. The duration is 5-7 seconds.
summary: On October 18, 1952, at 9:44 p.m., journalist Keith Hooper observed a large, greenish-white, cigar-shaped object over the Adelaide Hills that made a sharp upward turn and vanished rapidly.
title: **Cigar-Shaped Object with Sharp Turn Seen Over Adelaide Hills**

name: **Disc-Shaped Objects Seen by RAF Pilots, Unsuccessful Jet Interception**
description: **October 21, 1952, Afternoon** - Flight Lt. Michael Swiney and a student pilot, Royal Navy Lt. David Crofts, are flying a Meteor T.7 trainer out of **RAF Little Rissington, Gloucester, England**, for a high-altitude navigation exercise at 35,000 feet. Not long after breaking out of a cloud during a climb at 13,000-14,000 feet, they see **three circular, white objects** in front of them. As the aircraft get closer and turns to avoid them, the objects become visible as **discs**. They disappear quickly when the pilot looks away briefly. **Two Meteor F.8 fighters are scrambled from RAF Tangmere [now closed] in West Sussex to chase three unknown radar targets moving at 3,000 mph but fail to intercept them**.
location: RAF Little Rissington, Gloucester, England; RAF Tangmere, West Sussex, England
summary: In the afternoon of October 21, 1952, RAF pilots near Little Rissington saw three disc-shaped objects, which disappeared quickly; scrambled jets from RAF Tangmere failed to intercept radar targets moving at 3,000 mph.
title: **Disc-Shaped Objects Seen by RAF Pilots, Unsuccessful Jet Interception**

name: **Ruppelt Briefing at Los Alamos on UFOs and Radiation Detection**
description: **October 23, 1952** - Ruppelt holds a briefing on UFOs at **Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory, New Mexico**. Afterward Assistant Director for Scientific Personnel William H. Crew arranges a special meeting for Ruppelt and Col. Bower with seven people from the laboratory. Several of them have evidence that there is a **possible correlation between sightings of UFOs and unusual radiation detection**.
location: Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory, New Mexico, USA
summary: On October 23, 1952, Ruppelt briefed personnel at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory on UFOs, followed by a meeting where evidence of a potential link between UFO sightings and unusual radiation detection was discussed.
title: **Ruppelt Briefing at Los Alamos on UFOs and Radiation Detection**

name: **National Security Agency (NSA) Created**
description: **October 24, 1952** - President Truman signs National Security Council Directive 6, a 7-page document that eliminates the Armed Forces Security Agency and **creates the National Security Agency**. The existence of the NSA is not known to the public due to its classification. The NSA is responsible for global monitoring, collection, and processing of information for foreign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes. NSA inherits Project Shamrock from the AFSA and collection of UFO data, probably in 1953.
summary: On October 24, 1952, President Truman's National Security Council Directive 6 established the highly secret National Security Agency (NSA), responsible for global intelligence and counterintelligence, which would later inherit UFO data collection.
title: **National Security Agency (NSA) Created**

name: **Silent, Bright Light Zigzagging Near USS Curtiss**
description: **Late October 1952, Night** - Radioman Tom Kramer is serving aboard the **USS Curtiss**, the AEC flagship for Ivy Mike at Elugelab Atoll. Kramer and other crewmen see a **round, silent, bright white light** that is motionless at first, then starts **zigzagging for less than 10 seconds** and takes off at high speed.
location: Elugelab Atoll, Marshall Islands (near USS Curtiss)
summary: In late October 1952, crewmen aboard the USS Curtiss near Elugelab Atoll observed a round, silent, bright white light that zigzagged briefly before accelerating away rapidly.
title: **Silent, Bright Light Zigzagging Near USS Curtiss**

name: **White Light Hovering and Ascending Near USS Fletcher**
description: **Late October 1952, 3:45 a.m.** - Seaman Abelardo Marquez, posted on the **USS Fletcher near Eniwetak Atoll** for the Ivy Mike test, notices the ship moving at full speed due to a **round white light** above it. Marquez sees it descending, then stopping and **hovering** about 40°-45° above the horizon, perhaps one-half mile from the ship. Capt. Grover L. Rawlings says the light is not tracked on radar. After about 4-5 minutes, the light takes off straight up at the same speed it had descended.
location: Near Eniwetak Atoll, Marshall Islands (USS Fletcher)
summary: In late October 1952, at 3:45 a.m., crew on the USS Fletcher near Eniwetak Atoll observed a round white light that descended, hovered, was not detected on radar, and then ascended rapidly.
title: **White Light Hovering and Ascending Near USS Fletcher**

name: **Cigar-Shaped Object Lands Briefly at Marignane Airport, France**
description: **October 27, 1952, 2:03 a.m.** - Customs officer Gabriel Gachignard observes a **cigar-shaped object land briefly on a runway of the airport at Marignane, Bouches-du-Rhône, France**, 300 feet away, producing a dull sound. The object is dark with **four lighted windows**. It takes off with a '**swish**' and a shower of sparks when he runs toward it.
summary: On October 27, 1952, at 2:03 a.m., a customs officer at Marignane Airport, France, saw a dark, cigar-shaped object with four lighted windows land briefly, making a dull sound before taking off with a swish and sparks.
title: **Cigar-Shaped Object Lands Briefly at Marignane Airport, France**

name: **CIA Scientific Advisory Panel on UFOs (Robertson Panel) Convened**
description: **January 14-18, 1953** - The **CIA convenes a Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects** under the chairmanship of physicist H. P. Robertson. Other members include Samuel Goudsmit, Luis Alvarez, Allen Dulles, Thornton Page, and J. Allen Hynek (as a consultant). The panel is tasked to evaluate available evidence and assess the potential threat of UFOs to US security. They review films and sighting reports, including the Montana film and the Utah film analyzed by the Navy.
summary: From January 14-18, 1953, the CIA convened the Robertson Panel, a scientific advisory group led by H. P. Robertson, to evaluate UFO evidence and assess security threats.
title: **CIA Scientific Advisory Panel on UFOs (Robertson Panel) Convened**

name: **Robertson Panel Final Report Issued, Debunking Campaign Recommended**
description: **January 17, 1953** - The final day of the Robertson Panel. The panel reviews Robertson's draft report (Berkner has already seen it) and puts it into final form. The scientists agree that most sightings can be explained, and the rest a waste of effort. They reject Fournet's UFO reports and the Navy analysis of the Utah film. Because of the perceived overload of low-grade reports distracting from potential hostile objects, the Air Force should embark on a **debunking campaign** using scientific pronouncements and media, including Walt Disney Inc. animated cartoons. Civilian UFO groups should be watched for subversive potential. The report remains classified for some time.
summary: On January 17, 1953, the Robertson Panel finalized its report, recommending a debunking campaign by the Air Force using media to reduce public interest in UFOs and suggesting surveillance of civilian UFO groups.
title: **Robertson Panel Final Report Issued, Debunking Campaign Recommended**

name: **Blimp-Like Object Maneuvers Over Guatemala City**
description: **January 17, 1953, 3:55 p.m.** - Geologist/salesman John Townsend Sackett is riding in a bus with about a dozen passengers near **Guatemala City, Guatemala**, when he observes a **brilliant greenish-gold object, shaped like the Goodyear blimp**, about twice the size of a DC-3. The object is traveling at about **400 mph** straight and level in a northwesterly direction at about **6,500 feet**. It almost stops in mid-flight then rises vertically about 1,500 feet, hovers for about 2 seconds, then immediately resumes flight at a new altitude. The object is lost to view because of intervening terrain.
summary: On January 17, 1953, at 3:55 p.m., a blimp-like, greenish-gold object was seen near Guatemala City, performing unusual maneuvers including near-stops and vertical ascents.
title: **Blimp-Like Object Maneuvers Over Guatemala City**

name: **Hynek's Consultancy with Air Force Named 'Project Henry'**
description: **January 18, 1953** - Upon Hynek's return to Ohio State University from the Robertson Panel, he and his new research assistant Jennie Zeidman come up with the name '**Project Henry**' to describe his consultancy with the Air Force. It is based on the Flit bug-spray advertisement. Hynek regularly receives UFO reports and travels to the Blue Book facility at Wright-Patterson.
location: Ohio State University, Columbus, Ohio, USA; Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, USA
summary: On January 18, 1953, J. Allen Hynek and his assistant Jennie Zeidman named his Air Force consultancy 'Project Henry,' and he began regularly receiving UFO reports for analysis and visiting Project Blue Book.
title: **Hynek's Consultancy with Air Force Named 'Project Henry'**

name: **Robertson Mentions Meeting with 'NSA group'**
description: **January 20, 1953** - Robertson writes a letter to Chadwell, saying 'perhaps that'll take care of the Forteans for a while' and mentions an **upcoming meeting with the 'NSA group' on February 5**.
summary: On January 20, 1953, H. P. Robertson mentioned an upcoming meeting with an 'NSA group' in a letter to Chadwell.
title: **Robertson Mentions Meeting with 'NSA group'**

name: **Eisenhower Sworn In as President**
description: **January 20, 1953** - Dwight D. Eisenhower is sworn in as president.
summary: On January 20, 1953, Dwight D. Eisenhower was inaugurated as President of the United States.
title: **Eisenhower Sworn In as President**

name: **Patent Filed for Disc-Shaped VTOL Aircraft**
description: **January 23, 1953** - Lockheed employee Nathan C. Price files a patent for a **disc-shaped aircraft capable of landing or taking off vertically (VTOL)**. It is never built, but it is designed for long-range flights at speeds up to Mach 4, with a ceiling around 100,000 feet.
summary: On January 23, 1953, Lockheed employee Nathan C. Price patented a design for a disc-shaped VTOL aircraft intended for high-speed, high-altitude, long-range flight, though it was never constructed.
title: **Patent Filed for Disc-Shaped VTOL Aircraft**

name: **Ruppelt Briefs 4602nd AISS and Requests Transfer to Air Defense Command**
description: **January 24, 1953** - Ruppelt travels to **Ent AFB [now the US Olympic Training Center] in Colorado Springs, Colorado**, to brief the **4602nd AISS** on how they might help Blue Book investigate UFOs. He also requests to transfer to Air Defense Command here after his time at Blue Book is up.
location: Ent AFB (US Olympic Training Center), Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA
summary: On January 24, 1953, Ruppelt briefed the 4602nd AISS at Ent AFB on assisting Project Blue Book and requested a transfer to Air Defense Command.

name: **Air Force Claims Keyhoe's UFO Book Based on Cleared Intelligence Records**
description: **January 26, 1953** - Air Force Press Officer Albert M. Chop writes a letter to Keyhoe's publisher Henry Holt & Co., declaring that **all the sighting reports he is using for his upcoming Flying Saucers from Outer Space were cleared and made available to him from Air Technical Intelligence records**.
summary: On January 26, 1953, the Air Force stated that the UFO sighting reports used by Donald Keyhoe in his upcoming book were cleared and sourced from Air Technical Intelligence records.
title: **Air Force Claims Keyhoe's UFO Book Based on Cleared Intelligence Records**

name: **White Disc with Shimmering Edges Seen Near Point Mugu, California**
description: **January 28, 1953, 1:06 p.m.** - R. W. Love and a Mr. Ferrenti, while retrieving radio-controlled drones on a boat 1,100 yards offshore and south of **Naval Air Station Point Mugu [now Naval Base Ventura County] near Oxnard, California**, see a **white, flat disc with fuzzy or shimmering edges** rapidly approach from the northwest flying straight.
location: Offshore Naval Air Station Point Mugu, California, USA
summary: On January 28, 1953, at 1:06 p.m., near Point Mugu, California, two individuals observed a white, flat disc with shimmering edges rapidly approaching from the northwest.
title: **White Disc with Shimmering Edges Seen Near Point Mugu, California**

name: **Navy P2V Neptune Attacked by Multiple UFOs Over Sea of Japan**
description: **April 14, 1953, 9:23-11:50 p.m.** - A **Navy P2V Neptune spy plane** on an ELINT mission over the **Sea of Japan (about 200 miles southeast of Vladivostok, Russia)** is paced and **attacked by 10 agile and highly maneuverable UFOs**. The objects make more than '70 aggressive non-firing passes' very close to the Navy aircraft for over an hour. The UFOs **transmit Morse Code light signals (the letter 'D')**. The objects are tracked on radar and by the Navy's ELINT systems for almost two and a half hours.
location: Sea of Japan (200 miles SE of Vladivostok, Russia)
summary: On April 14, 1953, between 9:23 and 11:50 p.m., a US Navy P2V Neptune over the Sea of Japan was reportedly paced and aggressively approached over 70 times by 10 maneuverable UFOs, which also transmitted Morse code light signals; the event was tracked by radar and ELINT systems.
title: **Navy P2V Neptune Attacked by Multiple UFOs Over Sea of Japan**

name: **Metallic Disc Approaches Airliner Over New Brunswick**
description: **April 16, 1953, 3:45 p.m.** - The crew of a commercial Maritime Central airliner flying at **9,000 feet above Chatham, New Brunswick**, watches a **metallic disc** approach their plane and pass underneath.
summary: On April 16, 1953, at 3:45 p.m., the crew of a Maritime Central airliner flying over Chatham, New Brunswick, observed a metallic disc approach and pass beneath their aircraft.
title: **Metallic Disc Approaches Airliner Over New Brunswick**

name: **Delta-Shaped Object Seen Over Communist Territory in Korea**
description: **April 19, 1953, 1:00 p.m.** - Four US Army reconnaissance observers in two aircraft see a **white, rounded, delta-shaped object 5-7 feet in diameter flying at 60-80 mph with a 'vibrating' motion over Communist-held territory in Korea**. An official G-2 Intelligence Report says the object is in the Old Baldy (Hill 266) and Pork Chop Hill areas. Radar supposedly tracks them also moving faster than sound (>767 mph).
location: Korea (Old Baldy/Hill 266 and Pork Chop Hill areas)
summary: On April 19, 1953, at 1:00 p.m., US Army observers in Korea sighted a delta-shaped object moving at low speed with vibration over Communist territory, while radar reportedly tracked similar objects at supersonic speeds.
title: **Delta-Shaped Object Seen Over Communist Territory in Korea**

name: **Cabell Becomes Deputy Director of the CIA**
description: **April 23, 1953** - Gen. Charles P. Cabell becomes deputy director of the CIA.
summary: On April 23, 1953, Gen. Charles P. Cabell was appointed as the deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
title: **Cabell Becomes Deputy Director of the CIA**

name: **Dome-Shaped Disc Seen Hovering Over Quebec River**
description: **April 23, 1953, 3:00 p.m.** - Two witnesses in **Iberville [now Saint-Jean-de-Richelieu], Quebec**, see a **disc the size of a car** approach their house while they are eating dinner. It stops 250 feet above the **Richelieu River** a bit more than a half-mile away. The man runs outside for a better look and sees that it as a **dome and is spinning as it hovers**. After 15 seconds it flies to the southwest and disappears.
summary: On April 23, 1953, at 3:00 p.m., two witnesses in Quebec observed a car-sized, dome-shaped disc spinning as it hovered above the Richelieu River before flying southwest and disappearing.
title: **Dome-Shaped Disc Seen Hovering Over Quebec River**

name: **Flawed CAA Report on 1952 Washington National Airport Radar Returns**
description: **May 1953** - A **flawed CAA report states the July 1952 Washington National Airport radar returns were weather targets**.
location: Washington National Airport, Washington D.C., USA
summary: In May 1953, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) issued a report that controversially attributed the July 1952 radar returns at Washington National Airport to weather phenomena.
title: **Flawed CAA Report on 1952 Washington National Airport Radar Returns**

name: **CIA Shifts UFO Responsibility to OSI Physics and Electronic Division**
description: **May 1953** - CIA Assistant Director H. Marshall Chadwell transfers chief responsibility for keeping abreast of UFOs to OSI's Physics and Electronic Division. Todos M. Odarenko, chief of the division, proposes to call the project 'inactive' and devote only one part-time analyst and a file clerk to maintain a reference file.
summary: In May 1953, the CIA transferred primary responsibility for UFO monitoring to the OSI's Physics and Electronic Division, with a suggestion to reduce the project to 'inactive' status with minimal staffing.
title: **CIA Shifts UFO Responsibility to OSI Physics and Electronic Division**

name: **Air Force Manual 200-3: Handbook for Air Intelligence Officers Published**
description: **May 1953** - The Air Force publishes, under the signatures of Chief of Staff Gen. Hoyt S. Vandenberg and Air Adjutant General Col. Kenneth E. Thiebaud, **Air Force Manual 200-3, titled Handbook for Air Intelligence Officers**. It is classified Restricted and includes an illustration of an Air Force plane with three flying saucers, with the caption 'The Air Technical Intelligence center is responsible for the prevention of technological surprises'.
summary: In May 1953, the Air Force published the 'Handbook for Air Intelligence Officers' (AFM 200-3), a Restricted manual that included an illustration linking flying saucers to the responsibility of preventing technological surprises.
title: **Air Force Manual 200-3: Handbook for Air Intelligence Officers Published**

name: **White Light Evades F-94 Interceptor Over Labrador**
description: **May 1, 1953, 11:35 p.m.** - USAF pilot Capt. R. L. Emberry and radar operator 1Lt J. R. Morin are flying an **F-94 interceptor at 24,000 feet about 10 miles south of Goose Bay AFB [now CFB Goose Bay], Labrador**. Both men and a control tower operator see a **white light with a visible afterburner at 10,000 feet**. The F-94 pursues it, both climbing to 40,000 feet, but the object climbs out of sight after 30 minutes.
location: Near Goose Bay AFB, Labrador, Canada
summary: On May 1, 1953, at 11:35 p.m., a white light with an apparent afterburner was observed near Goose Bay AFB, Labrador, and evaded an F-94 interceptor which pursued it to 40,000 feet before the object climbed out of visual range.
title: **White Light Evades F-94 Interceptor Over Labrador**

name: **BOAC Comet Crash in India, UFO Rumors Persist**
description: **May 2, 1953** - BOAC Flight 783, a de Havilland Comet 1, crashes after taking off from **Calcutta-Dum Dum [now Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport], India**, killing all 43 on board. Witnesses observe the wingless Comet on fire. A British aviation investigator announces that the plane '**collided with a fairly heavy body**' and **UFO rumors persist for about a year**. However, leading investigators suspect structural failure.
location: Near Calcutta (Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport), India
summary: On May 2, 1953, a BOAC Comet crashed after takeoff from Calcutta, India, with a British investigator suggesting a collision with a 'heavy body,' leading to UFO rumors, though structural failure was suspected.

keywords: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport

title: **BOAC Comet Crash in India, UFO Rumors Persist**

name: **Football-Shaped Object Seen Near Goose Bay AFB**
description: **May 4, 1953, 1:50 a.m.** - A witness sees a **football-shaped, metallic object** caught in the glare of a rotating beacon near **Goose Bay AFB [now CFB Goose Bay], Labrador**. It is traveling south at high speed and a low altitude, and disappears into low-hanging stratus clouds. She hears a sound '**like tins striking together**'.
location: Near Goose Bay AFB, Labrador, Canada
summary: On May 4, 1953, at 1:50 a.m., a football-shaped, metallic object was observed near Goose Bay AFB, Labrador, moving south at high speed and low altitude before disappearing into clouds, accompanied by a metallic sound.
title: **Football-Shaped Object Seen Near Goose Bay AFB**

name: **Oblong Object with Concentric Rings Seen Near Yuma AFB**
description: **May 5, 1953, 9:45 a.m.** - Chemist Wells Alan Webb sees a **fuzzy-white oblong object** at an angle of 45° in the north near **Yuma AFB [now Marine Corps Air Station Yuma] near Yuma, Arizona**. Observed with naked eye and Polaroid glasses, it changes appearance, becomes circular, and **three concentric dark rings appear around the object** when viewed with Polaroid glasses. Webb speculates on the Faraday effect.
summary: On May 5, 1953, at 9:45 a.m., a chemist near Yuma AFB, Arizona, observed a fuzzy-white oblong object that later appeared circular with three concentric dark rings when viewed through Polaroid glasses, leading to speculation about the Faraday effect.
title: **Oblong Object with Concentric Rings Seen Near Yuma AFB**

name: **Lighted Dome Maneuvering Around Airliner Near Mackay, Queensland**
description: **May 10, 1953, 6:08 p.m.** - Capt. B. L. Jones is flying an Australian National Airways DC-3 just south of **Mackay, Queensland**. He radios the local control tower that a '**strange object like a lighted glass dome**' is maneuvering around his plane. He and his copilot watch the object for about 5 minutes during which time it climbs and dives at a speed of **200-700 mph**. Finally, it crosses the path of the aircraft and disappears swiftly to the west. Radar at Mackay tower shows no other aircraft nearby.
summary: On May 10, 1953, at 6:08 p.m., an airline captain near Mackay, Queensland, reported a 'lighted glass dome' maneuvering around his DC-3 at speeds of 200-700 mph before quickly disappearing; radar confirmed no other aircraft in the vicinity.
title: **Lighted Dome Maneuvering Around Airliner Near Mackay, Queensland**

name: **USN Pilot Reaches 753 mph in Douglas F4D Skyray**
description: **October 3, 1953** - USN pilot James B. Verdin reaches **753 mph in a Douglas F4D Skyray over the Salton Sea, California**.
location: Over the Salton Sea, California, USA
summary: On October 3, 1953, US Navy pilot James B. Verdin flew a Douglas F4D Skyray at 753 mph over the Salton Sea, California.
title: **USN Pilot Reaches 753 mph in Douglas F4D Skyray**

name: **UFO Discharges 'Angel Hair' Over Melbourne, Australia**
description: **October 9, 1953, 3:50 p.m.** - A UFO is seen at **Caulfield, Melbourne, Victoria**, discharging a **white trail described as 'strange shiney filaments' that cover wires and trees. A sample turns out to be a 'nylon-like amorphous mass with traces of magnesium, calcium, boron, and silicon.'** It shrinks significantly in an air-tight container.
summary: On October 9, 1953, at 3:50 p.m., a UFO over Melbourne, Australia, discharged a white, shiny, filamentous substance ('angel hair') that was analyzed and found to be a nylon-like material with various elements; it exhibited shrinkage in a sealed container.
title: **UFO Discharges 'Angel Hair' Over Melbourne, Australia**

name: **Radar Tracks Unidentified Objects Over Netherlands and UK**
description: **October 9, 1953, 4:30 p.m.** - Three unidentified objects are tracked on radar at **RAF Bawdsey [now Bawdsey Manor], Suffolk, England**, at an altitude of **36,000 feet above the Netherlands**. Soon they are tracked flying east to west over the **Harwich area**. Jets at **RAF Waterbeach [now Waterbeach Barracks], Cambridgeshire**, are scrambled but locate nothing. Airmen at Bawdsey see nothing but four contrails heading north. The objects then reverse and move back across the English Channel at **32,000-34,000 feet**. The apparent speed on the approach is 430 mph, increasing to 483 mph over the UK and 564 mph on the return.
location: Netherlands (airspace); RAF Bawdsey, Suffolk, England; Harwich area, England; RAF Waterbeach, Cambridgeshire, England; English Channel
summary: On October 9, 1953, at 4:30 p.m., radar at RAF Bawdsey tracked three unidentified objects over the Netherlands and UK, exhibiting directional changes and increasing speeds; scrambled jets found nothing visible.
title: **Radar Tracks Unidentified Objects Over Netherlands and UK**

name: **Object with Vapor Trail and Flashes Seen During Balloon Tracking in Minnesota**
description: **October 15, 1953, 10:10 a.m.** - During the tracking of a Project Grab Bag balloon launch, a **40-foot object leaving a brief vapor trail** is seen by three General Mills Aeronautical Lab research engineers near **Minneapolis, Minnesota**. It is traveling south at **1,100 mph** at about **40,000 ft altitude**. The object goes into a vertical dive, then **glows or flashes in the sun** two or three times for 1 second each, seen as a gray mass in the theodolite. It levels off and the vapor trail stops.
summary: On October 15, 1953, at 10:10 a.m., research engineers near Minneapolis observed a 40-foot object with a vapor trail moving at 1,100 mph and 40,000 feet during a balloon launch tracking; the object dove vertically and flashed in the sun.
title: **Object with Vapor Trail and Flashes Seen During Balloon Tracking in Minnesota**

name: **Menzel Requests Meeting with ATIC Officers**
description: **October 16, 1953** - Harvard astronomer Donald Menzel writes to USAF Director of Intelligence Gen. John A. Samford that he would like to meet with ATIC officers in Washington, D.C..
summary: On October 16, 1953, Harvard astronomer Donald Menzel requested a meeting with officers from the Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) in Washington, D.C..
title: **Menzel Requests Meeting with ATIC Officers**

name: **Cigar-Shaped Object Releases Smaller Objects Near Brigantine, New Jersey**
description: **October 16, 1953, 4:00-4:30 p.m.** - Emerson 'Slim' F. Morris watches a **large, cigar-shaped object** as it approaches **Brigantine, New Jersey**, from over the Atlantic. It **releases several smaller objects from both ends**. The smaller objects maneuver erratically.
summary: On October 16, 1953, between 4:00 and 4:30 p.m., a large cigar-shaped object was observed approaching Brigantine, New Jersey, over the Atlantic and releasing multiple smaller objects from its ends.
title: **Cigar-Shaped Object Releases Smaller Objects Near Brigantine, New Jersey**

name: **Luminous Object Changes Shape Over Saint-Émilion, France**
description: **December 9, 1953, 3:45 p.m.** - Charles Huaut sees a **luminous, golden, round object** poised motionless at a high altitude over **Saint-Émilion, Gironde, France**. After 10 minutes it noiselessly changes position and assumes the **form of several horseshoes enveloped in smoke trails**. Then it disappears.
summary: On December 9, 1953, at 3:45 p.m., a luminous, golden, round object was observed motionless over Saint-Émilion, France, before silently transforming into horseshoe shapes with smoke trails and then vanishing.
title: **Luminous Object Changes Shape Over Saint-Émilion, France**

name: **'Unorthodox, Metallic, Round Object' Encounters Swedish Airliner**
description: **December 15, 1953, 2:37 p.m.** - While flying a Transair Sweden DC-3 near **Hässleholm, Skåne, Sweden**, pilot Ulf Christiernsson and flight mechanic Olle Johansson encounter an '**unorthodox, metallic, symmetric, round object**' closing in on their aircraft for about 10 seconds. It passes about 1,970 feet under the DC-3 at an altitude of 7,055 feet. An investigation is launched, but a confession of a perfume company owner releasing balloons later emerges.
summary: On December 15, 1953, at 2:37 p.m., a Swedish airliner crew near Hässleholm encountered an 'unorthodox, metallic, symmetric, round object' passing close to their plane; the incident was later attributed to advertising balloons.
title: **'Unorthodox, Metallic, Round Object' Encounters Swedish Airliner**

name: **British Air Ministry Orders Classification of UFO Reports**
description: **December 16, 1953** - The **British Air Ministry sends orders to all RAF stations saying that UFO reports are to be classified 'Restricted' and personnel must not communicate any sighting information to unauthorized persons**. Reports must be sent to the air intelligence branch DDI (Tech).
summary: On December 16, 1953, the British Air Ministry mandated that all UFO reports from RAF stations be classified 'Restricted' and kept confidential, with reports directed to the DDI (Tech) branch.
title: **British Air Ministry Orders Classification of UFO Reports**

name: **Black Flying-Wing Object Observed Over California with Rapid Acceleration**
description: **December 16, 1953, 4:58 p.m.** - Lockheed Skunk Works chief Clarence L. 'Kelly' Johnson and his wife (near Agoura, California) and a Lockheed crew flying a WV-2 Warning Star (near Long Beach, California) independently observe a **black flying-wing (or ellipse or crescent-shaped) object** about 170-230 feet wide flying at about 15,000 ±2,000 feet altitude to the west, hovering about 30-60 miles away. At 5:04 p.m., the UFO suddenly takes off in a shallow climb accelerating to approximately **earth escape velocity (25,000 mph)** to the west over the Pacific, disappearing rapidly.
location: Agoura and Long Beach, California, USA (observations); Over the Pacific Ocean
summary: On December 16, 1953, at 4:58 p.m., Clarence 'Kelly' Johnson and a Lockheed crew separately witnessed a large, black flying-wing object hovering off the California coast, which then accelerated to escape velocity and disappeared over the Pacific Ocean.
title: **Black Flying-Wing Object Observed Over California with Rapid Acceleration**

name: **Swedish Investigation into Circular UFO Sighting**
description: **December 17, 1953** - After the crew of a Swedish airliner reports a **wingless circular UFO** over **Hässleholm, Sweden**, the Swedish Armed Forces orders a full-scale investigation. The object is described as 'entirely unorthodox, metallic, symmetrical, and circular.' Later reports claim it is a radiosonde balloon.
summary: On December 17, 1953, following a report by a Swedish airliner crew of a wingless circular UFO over Hässleholm, Sweden, the Swedish Armed Forces initiated a thorough investigation, although later it was suggested to be a radiosonde balloon.
title: **Swedish Investigation into Circular UFO Sighting**

name: **CIA Reviews Status of Government UFO Efforts**
description: **December 17, 1953** - A memo from Todos M. Odarenko, chief of the CIA/OSI physics and electronics division, condescendingly reviews the status of various government UFO efforts.
summary: On December 17, 1953, Todos M. Odarenko of the CIA/OSI issued a memo that critically reviewed the progress of different government initiatives concerning UFOs.
title: **CIA Reviews Status of Government UFO Efforts**

name: **USAF Recommends Standard Response for Unexplained UFO Sightings Investigated by 4602nd**
description: **December 23, 1953** - USAF Intelligence Col. George E. Perry recommends that when the **4602nd investigates a UFO sighting and it is not a conventional object**, personnel should state '**The information on this sighting will be analyzed by the Air Technical Intelligence Center at Dayton, Ohio,' and leave it at that**.
summary: On December 23, 1953, USAF Intelligence Col. George E. Perry advised a standard, limited response for unexplained UFO sightings investigated by the 4602nd, stating analysis would be done at ATIC.
title: **USAF Recommends Standard Response for Unexplained UFO Sightings Investigated by 4602nd**

name: **Silver Oval Objects in Formation Seen Over El Cajon, California**
description: **December 24, 1953, 8:04 a.m.** - US Navy Lts. J. B. Howard and L. D. Linhard, flying F9F-2 jet fighters, see **10 silver oval objects flying in formation at 450+ mph, straight and level, over El Cajon, California**.
summary: On December 24, 1953, at 8:04 a.m., two US Navy pilots in jet fighters observed 10 silver oval objects flying in formation at over 450 mph over El Cajon, California.
title: **Silver Oval Objects in Formation Seen Over El Cajon, California**

name: **Series of Articles Questions Air Force Openness About UFOs**
description: **December 26, 1953** - The first of a series of articles in the Washington (D.C.) Times-Herald by Richard Reilly **questions the Air Force's openness about UFOs**.
summary: On December 26, 1953, Richard Reilly began a series of articles in the Washington Times-Herald that questioned the transparency of the Air Force regarding UFOs.
title: **Series of Articles Questions Air Force Openness About UFOs**

name: **Keyhoe Confrontation with United Press Science Editor Over Debunking Series**
description: **December 29, 1953** - Keyhoe has a confrontation with Delos Smith, the science editor of the United Press wire service, and a UP executive editor. Smith is preparing a three-part series debunking Keyhoe's claims because a 'certain Air Force general swears your book is a complete fraud.' Keyhoe counters his arguments with documentation.
summary: On December 29, 1953, Donald Keyhoe confronted the science editor of United Press, who was preparing a series to debunk Keyhoe's UFO claims based on information from an Air Force general; Keyhoe responded with evidence.
title: **Keyhoe Confrontation with United Press Science Editor Over Debunking Series**

name: **Blinking Red Light Seen at Marine Corps Base Quantico**
description: **December 30, 1953, 9:05 p.m.** - Pfc Norman Viet, on guard duty at the tank park in **Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia**, watches a **blinking red light** about 18 inches in diameter moving slowly over a tree line about 200 feet away. It soon drops down out of sight. It is seen again later, rising and floating toward the tank shed. Viet says it is completely soundless. It reappears at 10:15 p.m., also witnessed by Sgt. Francis R. Salinder, prompting a base search. A red light reappears at midnight.
location: Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, USA
summary: On December 30, 1953, starting at 9:05 p.m., a blinking red light was observed multiple times at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, moving silently and prompting a base search.
title: **Blinking Red Light Seen at Marine Corps Base Quantico**

name: **Green Spheres Hover, Speed Away, Tracked on Radar Near Albuquerque**
description: **July 3, 1954** - Nine green spheres hover, speed away at **2,600 mph**, and are tracked on radar at **24,000 feet 20 miles north of Albuquerque, New Mexico**.
location: 20 miles north of Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA
summary: On July 3, 1954, nine green spheres were observed hovering and then accelerating to 2,600 mph near Albuquerque, New Mexico, tracked by radar at 24,000 feet.
title: **Green Spheres Hover, Speed Away, Tracked on Radar Near Albuquerque**

name: **Saucer-Shaped Object Seen by Passengers of Dutch Ocean Liner**
description: **July 3, 1954, 8:15 a.m.** - The captain, officers, and 463 passengers of a Dutch ocean liner watch a '**greenish-colored, saucer-shaped object about half the size of a full moon**' speed across the sky and disappear in clouds.
summary: On July 3, 1954, at 8:15 a.m., the crew and passengers of a Dutch ocean liner observed a greenish, saucer-shaped object about half the size of the moon speeding across the sky before disappearing into clouds.
title: **Saucer-Shaped Object Seen by Passengers of Dutch Ocean Liner**

name: **Bright Object with Smaller Objects Seen by Astronomer in England**
description: **July 8, 1954, 9:25 p.m.** - Amateur astronomer Harold Hill is at his observatory in **Orrell, Greater Manchester, England**, when he sees a bright star that resolves into a **bright, metallic globe with a cluster of 15-20 smaller, dimmer objects moving around**. Clouds obscure the view, and when they clear, he sees **two bright objects, gyrating and flashing and moving slowly around each other**. The observation lasts 25 minutes.
summary: On July 8, 1954, at 9:25 p.m., amateur astronomer Harold Hill in Orrell, England, observed a bright metallic globe surrounded by smaller objects, followed by two bright, gyrating objects over a 25-minute period.
title: **Bright Object with Smaller Objects Seen by Astronomer in England**

name: **Aerial Ships Seen Over Ireland and Britain**
description: **Around 743 (or 744 or 748): Aerial Ships Seen Over Ireland and Britain**. **Ireland (Ulster, Tigernach, Clonmacnoise, Four Masters, Lebar Gabála), later Teltown (County Meath, Ireland), then Clonmacnoise (Ireland), and finally Britain**. Accounts describe **ships with men aboard seen in the air over Ireland** [i]. Later versions detail a **single ship over Teltown** where a crewman throws and recovers a fishing-spear [i]. The scene shifts to **Clonmacnoise**, and then to **Britain**, with an anchor snagging on a church [i].
summary: Around 743, accounts describe aerial ships over Ireland and Britain, with details varying across different historical records [i].
title: **Aerial Ships Seen Over Ireland and Britain**

name: **Agobard of Lyon Writes About Magonia**
description: **812: Agobard of Lyon Writes About Magonia**. **Lyon, France**. Archbishop Agobard wrote about the pagan belief in **Magonia, a region from which ships navigated on clouds** [i]. He also recounts an incident of **peasants capturing alleged Magonian travelers** [i].
summary: In 812, Agobard of Lyon documented the belief in Magonia and an incident involving captured alleged Magonian travelers [i].
title: **Agobard of Lyon Writes About Magonia**

name: **Fireball with Hot Rays Seen Moving South**
description: **1547, December 15 - Mariners in the port of Hamburg, Germany, see a fireball moving to the south. Its rays are so hot that passengers cannot remain inside the ships. Thinking the vessels are about to burn, they hide and take cover.** (Simon Goulart, Thrésor d'histoires admirables et mémorables de nostre temps, Geneva, 1600, vol. 1, p. 55)
summary: On December 15, 1547, mariners in Hamburg, Germany, witnessed a southward-moving fireball with extremely hot rays.
title: **Fireball with Hot Rays Seen Moving South**

name: **'Frightening Vision' Over Nuremberg**
description: **1561, April 14 - Dusk. A 'frightening vision' is seen in the sky above Nuremberg, Germany, said to be observed by many. Printer Hans Glaser describes in his broadside many blood-red, blue, and black balls or discs near the Sun. 'They were three alongside each other, sometimes four in a square, and several alone, and between these balls blood-colored crosses' are seen. Two 'great pipes' (cannon) are also observed, and everything starts to 'fight against each other.' The battle lasts about one hour, then the burning balls fall to the earth and vanish on the ground.** Although cited as a possible early UFO report, the narrative is simply about a battle in the sky by phantom armies told as an allegory of what awaits an unrepentant humanity on Judgment Day. A meteorological cause is also possible. ('Nürnberger Flugblatt von 1561,' Wikipedia; Hans Glaser, Himmelserscheinung über Nürnberg am 14. April 1561, Holzschnitt, 1561; Carl Jung, Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies, Mentor ed., 1969, pp. 103-104, between pp. 120-121; Frank Johnson, 'Nuremberg 1561 UFO 'Battle' Debunked,' Ancient Aliens Debunked, December 12, 2012; Ulrich Magin, 'A UFO in the Year 1561,' Fortean Times 283 (February 2012): 40-42; Ulrich Magin, 'Ein UFO im Jahr 1561?'; '14th April 1561: The Nuremberg Celestial Phenomenon,' HistoryPod YouTube channel, April 13, 2015)
summary: On April 14, 1561, a 'frightening vision' was observed over Nuremberg, Germany, involving various aerial shapes and a perceived battle.
title: **'Frightening Vision' Over Nuremberg**

name: **Unusual Aerial Wonders and a Flat, Round Form**
description: **April 8, 1665: Unusual Aerial Wonders and a Flat, Round Form**. **Stralsund, Germany**. Numerous wonders were seen, including ships, birds, fire, smoke, and a **dark 'round flat form like a plate and like a big man's hat' hovering over a church** [i].
summary: On April 8, 1665, unusual aerial phenomena, including a flat, round form, were observed over Stralsund, Germany [i].
title: **Unusual Aerial Wonders and a Flat, Round Form**

name: **Meteoric Stream of Fire Observed**
description: **1745, July 14 - Astronomer George Costard observes a meteoric stream of fire whose trail persists for at least one hour at Standlake Broad west of Oxford, England.** ('Part of a Letter from the Reverend Mr. Geo. Costard to Mr. John Catlin, concerning a Fiery Meteor Seen in the Air on July 14, 1745,' Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 43 (1745): 522-524)
location: Standlake Broad west of Oxford, England
summary: On July 14, 1745, astronomer George Costard observed a long-lasting meteoric stream of fire near Oxford, England.
title: **Meteoric Stream of Fire Observed**

name: **Large Blue Fireball Explodes at Sea**
description: **1749, November 4 - 11:50 a.m. The crew of the HMS Montagu watches a large blue fireball, apparently low on the water, head directly toward them from the northeast and explode some 150 feet away from the ship, causing some damage to the mast, before it continues on toward the southwest. The incident takes place in the North Atlantic Ocean some 240 miles west of Cape Finisterre, Spain.** (Chalmers, 'An Account of an Extraordinary Fireball Bursting at Sea,' Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 46 (1752): 366-367; Chris Aubeck and Martin Shough, Return to Magonia: Investigating UFOs in History, Anomalist, 2015, pp. 67-75; Martin Shough and Wim van Utrecht, Redemption of the Damned, vol. 2, Anomalist, 2021, pp. 105-114)
location: North Atlantic Ocean, 240 miles west of Cape Finisterre, Spain
summary: On November 4, 1749, the crew of the HMS Montagu witnessed a large blue fireball explode near their ship in the North Atlantic.
title: **Large Blue Fireball Explodes at Sea**

name: **Automatic Writing Reveals Martian Canals and Inhabitants**
description: **1895, August - US psychical researcher James Hyslop begins investigating a case of automatic writing by Sarah Harper Cleaveland ('Mrs. Smead') in Onondaga County, New York. She keeps records of her planchette experiments and puts them at Hyslop's disposal. In August, she makes several references to the planet Mars and Jupiter. She provides a crude map of Jupiter's surface, and the planet is said to be the 'babies' heaven.' At the next sitting, she draws a map of Mars, the different zones named in the Martian language; she gives several communications about the inhabitants and the canals.** Martian revelations cease for another 5 years until September 1900, when the communications return in a developed state. She draws men, boats, houses, and flowers, named in Martian and written in hieroglyphic characters. Some of the sketches (a self-winding double clock) are very ingenious, while others (a Martian airship) are peculiar but unconvincing. (Hilary Evans, 'Martians of the 1890s,' IUR 11, no. 5 (Sept./Oct. 1986): 6-7)
summary: In August 1895, US psychical researcher James Hyslop investigated Sarah Harper Cleaveland's automatic writing, which included maps and descriptions of Mars and its inhabitants.

Murray, 'Remarkable Meteoric (?) Appearance,' London Times, September 4, 1895, p. 3; 'Remarkable Meteoric Appearance,' London Times, September 6, 1895, p. 8)
